description: A distortion that measures the level of the incoming audio, normalises it, adds noise, clips it and then restores the level it started with

params.text: Sets how much noise is mixed in, none at the far left
Sets how quickly the level-following envelope falls away, slow at the far left and fast at the far right; a faster fall follows the detail and gives a brighter, more broken result
Sets how hard the normalised audio is driven into the clipper, seven tenths of unity at the far left to sixteen times at the far right; the same gain is divided back out afterwards
Sets the shape of the clipper's corner, from a soft rounded bend at the far left to an almost square corner at the far right
Chooses where the noise goes: in the lower position it is subtracted from the level-following envelope, and in the upper position it is added to the normalised audio itself
In its upper position, the part of the sound below 150Hz is taken out before the distortion and put back at the main output, so the bass passes through clean

inputs.text: Takes over from the internal noise as the source of the grit; a polyphonic cable here is what makes the three outputs polyphonic

outputs.text: The distorted audio with the level restored, and with the bass added back when the bass split switch is up
The level-following envelope, as a positive voltage tracking the peak of the input
The difference between the distorted audio and the audio that went in, which is the distortion on its own with the original sound removed

notes: The module is mono until something is patched into the rasp input: the audio input is averaged down to one channel, and the channel count of all three outputs is taken from the rasp jack

inputs.1:
±5V · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads the module's own white noise.
